newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $20 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $20 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $20 per tonne higher Monday, on the heels of a strong performance in London overnight, trading sources said.

London cocoa prices were rose sharply early Monday, bolstered by heavy speculative short-covering. At the midsession break, the May contract was up 16 stg a tonne, to 962 stg, just off the high of 965 stg.
In fundamental news, Ivorian Commodities Minister Alain Gauze said on Monday the country's 1996/97 cocoa crop will be below one million tonnes.

Private estimates for the 96/97 Ivory Coast cocoa crop have been as high as 1.1 million tonnes while the government's official crop forecast, including mid-crop, published in December was 950,000 tonnes.
Gauze also told journalists at an International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) meeting in London the Ivory Coast has already sold around 800,000 tonnes, but has no more cocoa to sell.
In other news, a senior Ghana official at the ICCO meeting said Monday the country has sold just under 200,000 tonnes of its 1996/97 main crop cocoa still forecast at 300,000 tonnes.
John Newman, managing director of Ghana's cocoa board, said the country forecasts total crop at 330,000 tonnes including a light crop of around 30,000-35,000 tonnes.
On Friday, New York May cocoa futures closed $5 a tonne lower, at $1,325, having traded from $1,321 to $1,344. July fell $7, to $1,348.
On the charts, May near-term support was pegged at $1,316, with a key psychological level was seen at $1,300. Resistance was noted at $1,343-1,344.
